q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts from Corporation Tax are accounted for under Major Head:

options.B: 0021 - Taxes on Income other than Corporation Tax

e: Under the List of Major and Minor Heads, Major Head 0020 is the specific receipt head for Corporation Tax, distinct from other income taxes under 0021.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts from taxes on income other than Corporation Tax are accounted for under Major Head:

options.B: 0021 - Taxes on Income other than Corporation Tax

e: Major Head 0021 is expressly titled Taxes on Income other than Corporation Tax in the List of Major and Minor Heads, so such receipts fall under 0021.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts from Customs duties are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 0037 is the prescribed receipt head for Customs in the List of Major and Minor Heads, separate from Union Excise Duties under 0038.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts of the Government from other administrative services, not covered by the specific receipt heads, are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 0070, Other Administrative Services, is the residual receipt head for other administrative services not covered by a specific head.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the contributions and recoveries towards pension and other retirement benefits, received by the Government, are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 0071 - Contributions and Recoveries towards Pension and Other Retirement Benefits

e: Major Head 0071 is specifically titled Contributions and Recoveries towards Pension and Other Retirement Benefits, so those receipts are booked under it.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to Parliament is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2011 is the prescribed head for Parliament under General Services in the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on the administration of justice is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2014 is titled Administration of Justice, so expenditure on the administration of justice is classified under 2014.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to elections is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2015 is the prescribed head for Elections, covering expenditure relating to conduct of elections.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to audit is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2016 is titled Audit, so expenditure relating to audit is accounted for under 2016.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to land revenue is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2029 is the prescribed head for Land Revenue expenditure in the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on the Secretariat under General Services is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2052 is titled Secretariat - General Services, so secretariat expenditure under General Services falls under 2052.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on district administration is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2053 is the prescribed head for District Administration under General Services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to the police is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2055 is titled Police, distinct from 2056 Jails, so police expenditure is classified under 2055.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to public works, not covered by the functional major heads, is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2059, Public Works, is the head for public works expenditure not covered by functional major heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on general education is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2202 is titled General Education, distinct from technical education under 2203, so general education falls under 2202.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on medical and public health is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2210 is the prescribed head for Medical and Public Health under Social Services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on relief on account of natural calamities is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 2245 - Relief on account of Natural Calamities

e: Major Head 2245 is specifically titled Relief on account of Natural Calamities, so such relief expenditure is booked under 2245.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the grants-in-aid given by the Central Government to the State Governments are accounted for under Major Head:

options.D: 7601 - Loans and Advances to State Governments

e: Major Head 3601 is titled Grants-in-aid to State Governments, so Central grants-in-aid to States are accounted for under 3601, not 3602 for Union Territories.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on roads and bridges, as distinct from capital outlay on them, is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 5054 - Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges

e: The 3-series denotes revenue expenditure and the 5-series capital outlay; revenue expenditure on roads and bridges is therefore under 3054, not 5054.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans and advances given by the Central Government, which are not covered by any specific loan head, are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 7615, Miscellaneous Loans, is the residual loan head for Central loans not covered by any specific loan head such as 7610 or 6801.

q: Deposits of Local Funds on which interest is payable by the Government are accounted for in the Public Account of India under Major Head:
e: In the Public Account, the 83-series covers interest-bearing deposits; 8338 is the interest-bearing head for Deposits of Local Funds, while 8448 is non-interest-bearing.

q: In the Public Account of India, the deposits bearing interest, which are neither Civil Deposits nor Deposits of Local Funds, are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 8342 is the interest-bearing head for Other Deposits in the Public Account, distinct from Civil Deposits and Local Funds deposits.

q: In the Public Account of India, the deposits not bearing interest, which are neither Civil Deposits nor Deposits of Local Funds, are accounted for under Major Head:
e: In the Public Account, the 84-series covers deposits not bearing interest; 8449 is the non-interest-bearing head for Other Deposits.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the balances of permanent cash imprest held by Government officers are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 8672 is specifically titled Permanent Cash Imprest, so balances of permanent cash imprest held by officers are booked under 8672.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the miscellaneous Government accounts, such as the adjustment of cash balances, are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 8680, Miscellaneous Government Accounts, covers miscellaneous government accounts including adjustment of cash balances.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for power projects are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 6801 is titled Loans for Power Projects in the 6-series loan heads, distinct from revenue head 2801 and capital head 4801.

q: In the accounts of a State Government, the grants-in-aid received by it from the Government of India are accounted for, on the receipts side, under Major Head:

options.D: 6003 - Internal Debt of the State Government

e: From the State side, grants received from the Government of India are receipts under 1601, Grants from Government of India; 3601 is the Centre giving grants to States.

q: In the classification of Government accounts, Minor Head '800' is commonly opened under the various Major Heads to account for:

options.A: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India only
options.C: Recoveries of expenditure, shown as deduct entries
options.D: Other receipts or other expenditure not covered by any specific minor head

e: Minor Head 800 is the standard residual minor head opened under major heads for other receipts or other expenditure not covered by a specific minor head.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Major Head 8338 from Major Head 8448 in the Public Account of India?

options.A: Major Head 8338 covers Deposits of Local Funds bearing interest, while Major Head 8448 covers Deposits of Local Funds not bearing interest
options.B: Major Head 8338 covers Civil Deposits bearing interest, while Major Head 8448 covers Civil Deposits not bearing interest
options.C: Major Head 8338 is operated in the Consolidated Fund of India, while Major Head 8448 is operated in the Public Account of India
options.D: Major Head 8338 covers the deposits of local funds of the Union Government only, while Major Head 8448 covers those of the State Governments only

e: Both heads are for Deposits of Local Funds in the Public Account, but 8338 is in the interest-bearing section and 8448 in the non-interest-bearing section.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Major Head 3601 from Major Head 3602 in the Government system of classification of accounts?

options.A: Major Head 3601 covers loans to State Governments, while Major Head 3602 covers grants-in-aid to Union Territory Governments
options.B: Major Head 3601 covers grants-in-aid to State Governments, while Major Head 3602 covers grants-in-aid to Union Territory Governments
options.C: Major Head 3601 covers grants-in-aid to Union Territory Governments, while Major Head 3602 covers grants-in-aid to State Governments
options.D: Major Head 3601 is operated in the accounts of a State Government, while Major Head 3602 is operated in the accounts of the Union Government

e: Major Head 3601 covers grants-in-aid to State Governments and 3602 covers grants-in-aid to Union Territory Governments, as per their titles in the List.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'impact' of a tax from its 'incidence'?

options.A: The impact of a tax is the final burden borne by the person who ultimately pays it, while its incidence is the first point at which it is collected
options.B: The impact and the incidence of a tax are two names for one and the same burden, falling always on the same person
options.C: The impact of a tax is its first point of contact with the taxpayer, while its incidence is the point of its final resting place after shifting
options.D: The impact of a tax can never be shifted to another person, while its incidence is shifted in every case

e: Impact is the first point of contact where a tax is initially paid, while incidence is its final resting place after shifting; hence the stated distinction is correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the ability-to-pay approach to taxation from the benefit approach?

options.A: Under the ability-to-pay approach, a person is taxed in proportion to the benefits he receives from public expenditure
options.B: Under the benefit approach, a person is taxed strictly according to his income and wealth, irrespective of the benefits received
options.C: The two approaches are identical, both requiring the tax burden to be distributed in proportion to income
options.D: Under the ability-to-pay approach, a person is taxed according to his capacity to pay, while under the benefit approach he is taxed in proportion to the benefits received by him from public expenditure

e: Ability-to-pay taxes a person according to his capacity to pay, while the benefit approach taxes him in proportion to benefits received from public expenditure.

q: A tax is described as 'progressive' when:

options.A: The rate of tax increases as the tax base, such as income, increases
options.B: The rate of tax decreases as the tax base increases
options.C: The same rate of tax is applied to all taxpayers, irrespective of the size of the tax base
options.D: The amount of tax payable remains the same for every taxpayer, irrespective of the tax base

e: A progressive tax is defined by a rate that rises as the tax base, such as income, rises, so higher bases bear a higher percentage.

q: Which of the following pairs of Major Heads is correctly matched in the Government system of classification of accounts?

options.C: 0037 - Corporation Tax and 0038 - Taxes on Income other than Corporation Tax

e: In the List, 0037 is Customs and 0038 is Union Excise Duties; the other pairings reverse or misstate these prescribed titles.

q: 'Pump priming' in public finance refers to:

options.A: Continuous deficit spending by the Government to compensate for a permanent deficiency of private demand in the economy
options.B: Financing of the fiscal deficit of the Government through market borrowings and treasury bills
options.C: A relatively small, one-time injection of Government spending intended to revive private investment and set the economy moving again
options.D: An increase in taxation by the Government intended to withdraw purchasing power and curb inflation

e: Pump priming is a small, temporary injection of government spending meant to revive private investment and restart economic activity, not permanent deficit spending.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four canons of taxation enunciated by Adam Smith?
e: Adam Smith gave only equality, certainty, convenience and economy; productivity is a later canon added by subsequent writers, not one of Smith's four.

q: The canon of certainty in taxation requires that:

options.A: The tax payable by a person, and the time and manner of its payment, should be clear, plain and certain, and not arbitrary
options.B: The tax should be collected at the time and in the manner most convenient to the contributor
options.C: The cost of collecting the tax should be as small as possible in proportion to its yield
options.D: Every person should contribute to the revenue of the State in proportion to his ability to pay

e: The canon of certainty requires the tax, and its time and manner of payment, to be clear, plain and certain to the taxpayer, not arbitrary.

q: The 'displacement effect' in the growth of public expenditure, associated with Peacock and Wiseman, refers to:

options.A: The displacement of private investment by Government borrowing in the capital market
options.B: A step-like increase in public expenditure during a social disturbance, such as a war, after which the expenditure does not return to its earlier lower level
options.C: The displacement of tax revenue from the States to the Centre following a tax reform
options.D: The transfer of expenditure from the revenue account to the capital account of the Government

e: Peacock and Wiseman's displacement effect is the step-like rise in public expenditure during a war or disturbance, after which it does not return to the earlier level.

q: The Planning, Programming and Budgeting System (PPBS) is primarily characterised by:

options.A: Budgeting strictly by the objects of expenditure, such as salaries, travel and stores, without reference to programmes
options.B: Providing in each year's budget only a small incremental addition over the expenditure of the previous year
options.C: Linking expenditure to programmes and objectives, with an analysis of the costs and benefits of alternative ways of achieving them over a multi-year horizon
options.D: Justifying every programme and item of expenditure afresh from a zero base in each year's budget

e: PPBS links spending to programmes and objectives and analyses costs and benefits of alternatives over a multi-year horizon, unlike line-item or zero-based budgeting.

q: The 'Key Features of Budget' document, presented along with the Union Budget, primarily presents:

options.A: The detailed Demands for Grants of each Ministry and Department
options.B: The audited Finance Accounts and Appropriation Accounts of the previous year
options.C: The full text of the Finance Bill giving effect to the taxation proposals
options.D: The salient features and highlights of the Budget proposals at a glance

e: Key Features of Budget is a budget document summarising the salient features and highlights of the budget proposals at a glance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure relating to elections is accounted for under Major Head 2015.
2. In the same system, the expenditure relating to audit is accounted for under Major Head 2016.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements match the List: elections are under Major Head 2015 and audit under Major Head 2016, so both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Deposits of Local Funds bearing interest are accounted for in the Public Account of India under Major Head 8338.
2. Other Deposits not bearing interest are accounted for in the Public Account of India under Major Head 8342.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct as 8338 is interest-bearing Local Funds deposits; statement 2 is wrong because 8342 is interest-bearing Other Deposits, the non-interest head being 8449.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Grants-in-aid to Union Territory Governments are accounted for under Major Head 3601.
2. Loans for Power Projects are accounted for under Major Head 6801.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is wrong because 3601 is for State Governments, not Union Territories; statement 2 is correct because loans for power projects are under 6801.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The canon of convenience requires that a tax should be levied and collected at the time and in the manner most inconvenient to the taxpayer, so that its payment is ensured.
2. The canon of economy requires that the cost of collecting a tax should be allowed to exceed the yield of the tax.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements reverse the canons: convenience means collection at a time and manner convenient to the taxpayer, and economy requires collection cost to be low, not exceed yield.

q: A fire in a railway stores depot destroys a large quantity of Government stores, and the responsibility for the loss has not yet been finally fixed. Under the principles of Government financial control, the loss is required in the first instance to be:

options.A: Written off at once by the depot officer, without any report to higher authority
options.B: Held under a suspense head and reported to Audit only at the close of the financial year
options.C: Promptly reported by the subordinate authority to the next higher authority and to the Audit/Accounts authorities, even before the responsibility for the loss is finally determined
options.D: Recovered in full from the storekeeper in charge, regardless of whether any negligence is established against him

e: Government financial rules require losses of government property to be promptly reported to the next higher authority and to Audit/Accounts, even before responsibility is finally fixed.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on crop husbandry is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2401 is titled Crop Husbandry, so revenue expenditure on crop husbandry is classified under 2401.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on animal husbandry is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2403 is the prescribed revenue head for Animal Husbandry, distinct from 2401 Crop Husbandry and 2404 Dairy Development.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on forestry and wild life is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2406 is titled Forestry and Wild Life, so revenue expenditure on forestry and wild life falls under 2406.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on special programmes for rural development is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2501 is specifically titled Special Programmes for Rural Development, so such programme expenditure is booked under 2501.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on rural development programmes other than the special programmes is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2515, Other Rural Development Programmes, is the residual head for rural development programmes other than special programmes under 2501.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure relating to power is accounted for under Major Head:

options.C: 2045 - Other Taxes and Duties on Commodities and Services

e: Major Head 2801 is titled Power in the revenue section, distinct from capital outlay on power projects under 4801, so revenue expenditure on power falls under 2801.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on ports and light houses is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3051 is the prescribed revenue head for Ports and Light Houses, distinct from 3052 Shipping and 3053 Civil Aviation.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on civil aviation is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3053 is titled Civil Aviation, so revenue expenditure on civil aviation is classified under 3053.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on road transport is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3055 is the prescribed revenue head for Road Transport under transport services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on transport services not covered by the specific transport major heads is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3075, Other Transport Services, is the residual revenue head for transport services not covered by specific heads like 3051 to 3056.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on scientific research other than agricultural, industrial and atomic energy research is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3425 - Other Scientific Research is the residual head in the List of Major and Minor Heads for scientific research other than agricultural (2415), industrial and atomic energy (3401) research, so the expenditure is booked under 3425.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on the Secretariat under Economic Services is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3451 is titled Secretariat - Economic Services, so secretariat expenditure under Economic Services falls under 3451.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure relating to tourism is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 3452 is the prescribed revenue head for Tourism under Economic Services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on urban development is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2217 is titled Urban Development, distinct from 2216 Housing and 2215 Water Supply and Sanitation, so urban development falls under 2217.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on information and publicity is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 2225 - Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities

e: Major Head 2220 is the prescribed revenue head for Information and Publicity under Social Services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on the welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities is accounted for under Major Head:

options.D: 2225 - Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities

e: Major Head 2225 is specifically titled Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities, so that welfare expenditure falls under it.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure relating to labour and employment is accounted for under Major Head:

options.B: 2225 - Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities

e: Major Head 2230 is titled Labour and Employment, so revenue expenditure on labour and employment is classified under 2230.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on village and small industries is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Major Head 2851 is the prescribed revenue head for Village and Small Industries, distinct from 2852 Industries.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on currency, coinage and mint is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4047 - Capital Outlay on Other Fiscal Services
options.C: 4046 - Capital Outlay on Currency, Coinage and Mint

e: Major Head 4046 is titled Capital Outlay on Currency, Coinage and Mint in the 4-series capital heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on police is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4058 - Capital Outlay on Stationery and Printing
options.C: 4046 - Capital Outlay on Currency, Coinage and Mint

e: Major Head 4055 is the prescribed head for Capital Outlay on Police, distinct from revenue police expenditure under 2055.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on medical and public health is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4210 - Capital Outlay on Medical and Public Health
options.C: 4215 - Capital Outlay on Water Supply and Sanitation

e: Major Head 4210 is titled Capital Outlay on Medical and Public Health, the capital counterpart of revenue head 2210.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on water supply and sanitation is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4210 - Capital Outlay on Medical and Public Health
options.B: 4215 - Capital Outlay on Water Supply and Sanitation
options.D: 4225 - Capital Outlay on Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities

e: Major Head 4215 is the prescribed head for Capital Outlay on Water Supply and Sanitation.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on the welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4220 - Capital Outlay on Information and Publicity
options.B: 4235 - Capital Outlay on Social Security and Welfare
options.C: 4225 - Capital Outlay on Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities
options.D: 4250 - Capital Outlay on Other Social Services

e: Major Head 4225 is the head for Capital Outlay on Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and Minorities.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on medium irrigation is accounted for under Major Head:

options.C: 4711 - Capital Outlay on Flood Control Projects

e: Major Head 4701 is titled Capital Outlay on Medium Irrigation, distinct from 4700 Major Irrigation and 4702 Minor Irrigation.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on power projects is accounted for under Major Head:

options.D: 4810 - Capital Outlay on New and Renewable Energy

e: Major Head 4801 is the prescribed head for Capital Outlay on Power Projects, distinct from revenue head 2801 and loan head 6801.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on ports and light houses is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 5054 - Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges
options.B: 5051 - Capital Outlay on Ports and Light Houses

e: Major Head 5051 is titled Capital Outlay on Ports and Light Houses in the 5-series transport capital heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on civil aviation is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 5051 - Capital Outlay on Ports and Light Houses

e: Major Head 5053 is the prescribed head for Capital Outlay on Civil Aviation, distinct from 5051 Ports and 5052 Shipping.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for crop husbandry are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6402 - Loans for Soil and Water Conservation

e: Major Head 6401 is titled Loans for Crop Husbandry in the 6-series loan heads, so loans for crop husbandry fall under 6401.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for food storage and warehousing are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6408 - Loans for Food Storage and Warehousing
options.D: 6515 - Loans for Other Rural Development Programmes

e: Major Head 6408 is specifically titled Loans for Food Storage and Warehousing, so such loans are booked under 6408.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Major Head 4701 from Major Head 4702 in the Government system of classification of accounts?

options.A: Major Head 4701 covers capital outlay on minor irrigation, while Major Head 4702 covers capital outlay on medium irrigation
options.B: Major Head 4701 covers capital outlay on medium irrigation, while Major Head 4702 covers capital outlay on minor irrigation
options.C: Major Head 4701 covers revenue expenditure on medium irrigation, while Major Head 4702 covers capital outlay on minor irrigation
options.D: Major Head 4701 is operated only in the accounts of the Union Government, while Major Head 4702 is operated only in the accounts of the State Governments

e: In the List, 4701 is Capital Outlay on Medium Irrigation and 4702 is Capital Outlay on Minor Irrigation; the reverse pairing is incorrect.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a specific tax from an ad valorem tax?

options.A: A specific tax is levied as a percentage of the value of the commodity, while an ad valorem tax is levied per unit of its weight or quantity
options.B: A specific tax is levied only on imports, while an ad valorem tax is levied only on domestic production
options.C: A specific tax is levied per unit of the weight, quantity or measurement of the commodity, while an ad valorem tax is levied as a percentage of its value
options.D: A specific tax can be shifted to another person, while an ad valorem tax can never be shifted

e: A specific tax is charged per unit of weight, quantity or measurement, while an ad valorem tax is charged as a percentage of the value of the commodity.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes tax evasion from tax avoidance?

options.A: Tax evasion is a lawful arrangement for reducing tax liability, while tax avoidance is an offence punishable under the tax laws
options.B: Tax evasion and tax avoidance are two names for the same practice, both being offences under the tax laws
options.C: Tax avoidance consists of concealing income and falsifying accounts, while tax evasion consists of arranging transactions within the framework of the law
options.D: Tax evasion is the illegal non-payment of tax by concealing income or falsifying records, while tax avoidance is the lawful arrangement of transactions so as to reduce tax liability within the framework of the law

e: Tax evasion is illegal non-payment by concealment or falsification, while tax avoidance is lawfully arranging affairs within the law to reduce tax liability.

q: A tax is described as 'degressive' when:

options.A: The rate of tax rises with the size of the tax base, but less than proportionately, so that the progression becomes milder at the higher levels of the base
options.B: The rate of tax falls continuously as the tax base increases, at all levels of the base
options.C: The same fixed amount of tax is payable by every taxpayer, irrespective of the size of the tax base
options.D: The rate of tax rises more than proportionately at every level of increase in the tax base

e: A degressive tax rises with the base but less than proportionately, so progression becomes milder at higher levels, unlike a continuously falling regressive rate.

q: A tax is described as 'regressive' when:

options.A: The rate of tax increases as the tax base, such as income, increases
options.B: The rate of tax decreases as the tax base increases, so that the tax takes a smaller proportion of a larger tax base
options.C: The same rate of tax is applied to all taxpayers, irrespective of the size of the tax base
options.D: The amount of tax is fixed per unit of the commodity taxed, irrespective of its value

e: A regressive tax takes a decreasing proportion as the base increases, so its rate falls with a larger base and burdens lower bases relatively more.

q: In the Peacock-Wiseman analysis of the growth of public expenditure, the 'inspection effect' refers to:

options.A: The tendency of public expenditure to rise in steps during a war or other social disturbance and not to return to its earlier level afterwards
options.B: The concentration of public expenditure in the hands of the Central Government in a federal set-up
options.C: The revelation, during a period of disturbance and closer scrutiny of public affairs, of neglected problems and inadequacies in existing services, leading to new demands for public expenditure
options.D: The inspection of Government expenditure by the audit authorities before it is incurred

e: Peacock and Wiseman's inspection effect is the revelation during disturbance and scrutiny of neglected problems, creating new demands for public expenditure.

q: In the Peacock-Wiseman analysis of the growth of public expenditure, the 'concentration effect' refers to:

options.A: The concentration of the tax burden on a small number of large taxpayers
options.B: The tendency of expenditure to be concentrated in the closing months of the financial year
options.C: The concentration of audit objections on a small number of spending departments
options.D: The tendency, in a federal system, for the Central Government to grow faster than the State and local governments, so that public activity becomes increasingly concentrated at the Centre

e: The concentration effect is the tendency in a federation for the Central Government to grow faster than States and local bodies, concentrating public activity at the Centre.

q: Under the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the audit of the accounts relating to stores and stocks maintained by Government is provided for in:
e: Section 17 of the C and AG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 provides for audit of accounts relating to stores and stocks.

q: Under the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the audit of the receipts of the Government of India and of the States is provided for in:
e: Section 16 of the C and AG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 provides for audit of receipts of the Union and the States.

q: In audit, the use of statistical sampling primarily enables the auditor to:

options.A: Examine every voucher and transaction of the audited unit, without exception
options.B: Dispensing altogether with the need for professional judgement in audit
options.C: Select and examine a sample of items in a manner that permits a valid conclusion to be drawn about the whole population of transactions from which the sample is taken
options.D: Restrict the audit of a unit to the transactions of a single month selected by the audited unit itself

e: Statistical sampling lets the auditor examine a properly selected sample and draw a valid conclusion about the whole population, without examining every item.

q: The 'Statement of Revenue Forgone', presented with the Union Budget documents, primarily shows:

options.A: The revenue actually collected under each major head during the previous year
options.B: The arrears of tax revenue remaining uncollected at the close of the year
options.C: The subsidies paid by the Government to public sector undertakings during the year
options.D: The estimated revenue impact of the tax incentives, exemptions and deductions allowed under the tax laws, that is, the revenue the Government gives up by way of such concessions

e: The Statement of Revenue Forgone shows the estimated revenue impact of tax incentives, exemptions and deductions, that is revenue given up through such concessions.

q: The management of the public debt of the Central Government, and the issue and servicing of its market loans, is carried out on behalf of the Government by:

options.A: The Reserve Bank of India, as the Government's debt manager and banker
options.B: The Controller General of Accounts, Ministry of Finance
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Securities and Exchange Board of India

e: The Reserve Bank of India acts as banker and debt manager for the Central Government and manages its public debt, including issue and servicing of market loans.

q: The Detailed Demands for Grants of a Ministry or Department primarily contain:

options.A: The audited actuals of expenditure of the Ministry for the previous three years, as certified by the C&AG
options.B: The detailed estimates of expenditure under the various heads of account, together with explanations for important variations between the estimates and the actuals or previous estimates
options.C: The full text of the Appropriation Act relating to the Ministry
options.D: The replies of the Ministry to the audit paragraphs contained in the C&AG's Reports

e: Detailed Demands for Grants give detailed estimates under various heads with explanations for important variations from actuals or previous estimates.

q: The doctrine of 'functional finance', associated with Abba P. Lerner, holds that:

options.A: The Government budget must be balanced in every year, whatever the state of the economy
options.B: Public borrowing should be resorted to only for financing capital works that yield a direct monetary return
options.C: Fiscal measures should be judged by their effects on the economy, such as employment and price stability, and the budget should be used to maintain aggregate demand at the level needed for full employment, rather than being balanced as an end in itself
options.D: The functions of taxation and public expenditure should be divided between the Centre and the States strictly in proportion to their revenues

e: Lerner's functional finance judges fiscal measures by their effects on employment and price stability, using the budget to maintain demand for full employment, not annual balance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on crop husbandry is accounted for under Major Head 2401.
2. In the same system, the revenue expenditure on forestry and wild life is accounted for under Major Head 2403.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct as crop husbandry is under 2401; statement 2 is wrong because 2403 is Animal Husbandry and forestry and wild life is under 2406, so only statement 1 holds.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the compensation and assignments payable by the Government to local bodies and Panchayati Raj Institutions are accounted for under Major Head:

options.C: 3605 - Technical and Economic Co-operation with Other Countries
options.D: 3604 - Compensation and Assignments to Local Bodies and Panchayati Raj Institutions

e: Major Head 3604 is specifically titled Compensation and Assignments to Local Bodies and Panchayati Raj Institutions, so such payments fall under 3604.

q: The 'Principle of Maximum Social Advantage' in public finance, associated with Dalton, holds that public expenditure and taxation should be carried to the point where:

options.A: The marginal social benefit of public expenditure equals the marginal social sacrifice imposed by taxation
options.B: The total revenue of the Government exactly equals its total expenditure in every year
options.C: The burden of taxation is distributed equally among all citizens, irrespective of income
options.D: Public expenditure is increased continuously so long as any public need remains unmet

e: Dalton's maximum social advantage requires public expenditure and taxation to be pushed to where marginal social benefit equals marginal social sacrifice.

q: In the classification of the functions of public finance associated with Musgrave, the three branches or functions of the budgetary policy of the Government are:

options.A: Taxation, borrowing and printing of currency
options.B: Allocation of resources, distribution of income and wealth, and stabilisation of the economy
options.C: Revenue collection, expenditure control and audit of accounts

e: Musgrave classified budgetary policy into three functions: allocation of resources, distribution of income and wealth, and stabilisation of the economy.

q: A 'public good', in the theory of public finance, is characterised by:

options.A: Its supply exclusively by a Government department and not by any private agency
options.B: Its being provided free of charge to every citizen
options.C: Non-rivalry in consumption and non-excludability, so that one person's consumption does not reduce its availability to others and no one can be excluded from enjoying it
options.D: Its being financed wholly out of the proceeds of a single earmarked tax

e: A public good is non-rival and non-excludable: one person's consumption does not reduce availability to others and no one can be excluded from it.

q: 'Merit goods', in Musgrave's terminology, are goods:

options.A: Whose consumption is rival and excludable, like ordinary private goods
options.B: Exported to other countries in return for foreign exchange
options.C: Produced only by public sector undertakings
options.D: Whose consumption the Government encourages and subsidises, such as elementary education and preventive health care, because their social benefit exceeds what individual consumers, left to themselves, would provide for

e: Merit goods are those whose consumption government encourages and subsidises, like elementary education and preventive health, because social benefit exceeds private demand.

q: The 'Principle of Least Aggregate Sacrifice' in the distribution of the burden of taxation is associated with:
e: The principle of least aggregate sacrifice, requiring equal marginal sacrifice, is associated with Pigou in the theory of tax burden distribution.

q: The canon of simplicity in taxation, added by writers later than Adam Smith, requires that:

options.A: Every tax should yield a large and growing revenue to the Government
options.B: Every tax should be simple, plain and intelligible to the common taxpayer
options.C: The tax should be collected at the time most convenient to the taxpayer
options.D: The cost of collection of the tax should be the minimum possible

e: The canon of simplicity, added after Adam Smith, requires every tax to be simple, plain and intelligible to the common taxpayer.

q: The canons of taxation originally given by Adam Smith were later expanded by Findlay Shirras, who added to the list the canons of:
e: Findlay Shirras expanded Smith's canons by adding productivity, elasticity, diversity and simplicity to equality, certainty, convenience and economy.

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of:
e: The Committee on Public Undertakings was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of the Krishna Menon Committee.

q: The Controller General of Accounts, who is the principal accounting adviser to the Government of India on accounting matters, functions in:

options.A: The Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance
options.B: The Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance

e: The Controller General of Accounts is the principal accounting adviser to the Government of India and functions in the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance.

q: A principal consequence of the departmentalisation of Union Government accounts, under which accounts were separated from audit with effect from 1976, was that:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General began compiling the accounts of all Ministries himself
options.B: The Ministries and Departments of the Union Government became responsible for compiling their own accounts through their Pay and Accounts Offices, and the C&AG was relieved of that compilation work for the Union
options.C: The accounts of the Union and the States were merged into a single set of accounts
options.D: The audit of Government accounts was transferred from the C&AG to the Finance Ministry

e: After departmentalisation in 1976, Union Ministries compiled their own accounts through Pay and Accounts Offices, relieving the C and AG of Union compilation work.
